Towering white thunderheads stack twenty stories high above the weathered rooftops, their cathedral shadows swallowing the dusty street whole.
A vast cobalt dome stretches unbroken from flat horizon to flat horizon, making the town's false fronts look like scattered matchboxes.
Blazing orange and magenta pour across the western sky, setting every window in town afire with reflected light.
Pale lavender dawn spreads soft and wide above the sleeping rooftops, the church steeple a dark needle stitched into the quiet sky.
A black monsoon wall advances from the south, distant silver rain-curtains sweeping the plain toward the tiny huddled town.
A deep blue night sky salted with a thousand stars hangs low, the bright moon throwing sharp ink shadows across the empty street.
The noon sky burns bleached white and merciless, draining all color from the town below into a flat, heat-hammered stillness.
Long streaks of gold and copper cloud burn across the evening sky, the town below already sinking into early shadow.
Thousands of starlings wheel and surge in dark ribbons across the dusk sky, banking in unison above the silent rooftops.
A cold storm light flattens the plain, then one blazing shaft of sun breaks through and ignites the general store's tin roof.
Anvil-headed thunderheads glow brilliant white at their crowns and charcoal black at their bases, the town crouching small beneath them.
A wide clear sky of deep turquoise arches overhead, a single hawk riding a thermal high above the water tower.
Sunset pours molten copper and rose across half the sky, the other half still holding the faint blue ghost of afternoon.
A soft gray-lavender pre-dawn sky silences the town, rooftops edged faintly pink where the horizon has begun to remember the sun.
Green-tinged storm clouds press low over the street, the air dead still, rain-curtains visible on three sides of the trembling town.
The full moon rides high and cold in a blue-black sky dusted with stars, flooding the empty main street with silver light.
A white-hot sky beats down with no cloud for relief, the town below baked pale under the pitiless midday blaze.
Broad golden bands of cloud catch the last horizontal light, striping the vast sky above the town in layers of fire and shadow.
Hundreds of crows pour across the bruised dusk sky in ragged streams, circling the grain store and vanishing into the failing light.
A single blinding bar of sunlight cuts beneath the storm shelf, striking the saloon facade gold against the surrounding purple dark.
Massive thunderheads catch the late sun and glow like burning mountains while the town below sits in their cool deep shade.
A pellucid blue sky arches enormous and nearly cloudless overhead, one long white contrail of cirrus drifting slow above the livery stable.
Deep scarlet and violet flood the western sky at sunset, the town's silhouette a thin dark line of peaks and chimneys.
A luminous full moon climbs above the ridge, flooding the star-packed sky and turning the whole sleeping town to pewter and bone.
Rolling gray-green clouds swallow the horizon on every side, one golden break of storm-light spotlighting the lone water tower above town.
